newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST -Australian Sports News - Nov 6.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

The decisive 1996 Melbourne Cup win by Saintly propelled star trainer Bart Cummings into the history books following his astonishing training performance for his 10th cup victory. Flemington rose to applause as Cummings was heralded by Governor General Si William Deane, the Victorian Racing Club and Saintly's owner, businessman Dato Tan Chin Nam. Page 22.

Wallaby coach Greg Smith has introduced a radical code of conduct for the Australian squad's tour through the United Kingdom and Ireland, with fines of up to A$1500 for off-field breaches of discipline. Page 18.

Always receptive to a good idea, West Indian cricket coach Malcolm Marshall is considering fining his fast bowlers for no-balls after his pace quartet delivered 11 no-balls between them in the match against the Australian Cricket Board Chairman's XI on Moday. Page 18.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

With finishing touches by jockey Darren Beadman, the Bart Cummings "world-class horse" Saintly (6-1), careered away to take out the Melbourne Cup by two and a quarter lengths in the time of 3 minutes and 18.8 seconds for the 3,200-metre run. Page 48.

"A bridge too far" is how Irishman Ollie Lehane described his over-speculated galloper Oscar Schindler. In the lead-up to the Melbourne Cup the predictions were all giving Oscar Schindler a massive win, but on the scoreboard the 4-1 favourite finished 15th without ever featuring among the race leaders. Page 48.

Champion - yet still overwhelmed golfer - Karrie Webb will today meet fellow Queenslander Greg Norman at a press conference on the eve of the A$300,000 Australian Women's Open at Melbourne's Yarra Yarra course. High on the list of things to discuss, Webb will be enquiring about how to cope with the pressures of her new status and perhaps a game plan for the upcoming US women's tour. Page 45.
THE AGE

Cricketer Ricky Ponting's failure to grasp the number three position in the Australian batting order vacated by David Boon has left the way open for Steve Waugh to jump up the list for the Test series against the West Indies this summer. Page C16.

Jason Stoltenberg and Sandon Stolle led the Australian charge in round one of the Stockholm Open tennis tournament. Stoltenberg beat Norway's Christian Ruud 6-1, 6-7 (5-7), 6-1 and Stolle after losing the second set against Swede Jonas Bjorkman, came homestrongly to win 6-3, 4-6, 6-1. Page C16.

Australian surfing has suffered a blow following its chances of inclusion in the Sydney 2000 Olympics being described as "zilch" after Australian Olympic officials remain committed to keeping a close ceiling on the size of the games. Page C14.
HERALD SUN

Former Australian first-class cricket batsman David Boon lashed out at the media yesterday, accusing coverage of the Australian team's winless Indian tour as being overly negative. Boon said the team's performance in India was no indication of their chancs in the five-Test series against the West Indies this Summer. Page 78.

Australia's best performed woman golfer Jan Stephenson claimed she was hurt by rookie sensation Karrie Webb on the eve of the Australian Women's Open. Stephenson was dismayed Webb had focused on the champion's pin-up pose for a calendar rather than her distinguished playing record. Page 78.

Jockey Darren Beadman yesterday won his second Melbourne Cup on the back of Saintly without having to reach for his whip. Saintly's owner Dato Tan Chin Nam described Beadman's performance as "copybook", as it was close to a replica of the 1990 Beadman Melbourne Cup win on the Bart Cummings trained Kingston Rule. Page 74.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Bart Cummings shed a tear on the way to the Flemington winner's circle as he was about to be presented with his 10th Melbourne Cup following the heavenly performance of race triumph Saintly. The galloper eased from 7-1 to 8-1, easily winning over second paced Count Chivas (33-1) and Adelaide-based Skybeau (50-1), a close third. Page 72.

Giving evidence at the fourth day of his fraud trial, former New South Wales Rugby Union Boss Ken Elphick told the jury that he had "absolute authority" over a slush fund which had been set up to make secret payments for the benefit of Rugby. Page 70.

The New South Wales Rugby Union wants to cut up to two clubs by 1998 in the AAMI Cup premiership. The proposal, put forward as part of the Towards 2000 committee report, would involve two clubs either being dropped from the competition or being merged to form a 12-team roster. Page 64.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
